And a slight narrowing of the high-stakes cycle is borne out in recent polling on a generic congressional ballot.

DDHQ’s averages show Democrats with a 4-point advantage over Republicans on a generic ballot. That includes July polling from YouGov/The Economist, which found Democrats up 5 points in its latest survey, and from Morning Consult, which put Democrats up just 3 points. Last month, the average was closer to a 6- or 7-point edge for Democrats. [...] At this point in the 2018 cycle, when Democrats won big in the so-called blue wave, the generic ballot showed Democrats up by an average of 7 points or 8 points, DDHQ said, which is double the current edge.

results.content: When it comes to how they’re feeling about America, the picture is just as bad as how they feel about the two parties. According to YouGov/The Economist tracking data, 68 percent of registered independent voters say the economy is getting worse, higher than at any time in the last five years since July 2022, and 11 points higher than among registered voters overall. Similarly, 74 percent say that the country is on the wrong track, compared to 64 percent of registered voters overall.
